lessons.goal: 分辨單次成果、重複觀察與仍待查明的原因。

lessons.story:
In a fictional classroom test, a team's paper bridge holds twelve small blocks before bending. On a second attempt with the same design, a new bridge holds nine. The students want to keep only the first result because it makes their project look stronger.

The teacher asks them to record both attempts and compare how the bridges were made. One fold was slightly different, and the blocks may not have been placed in exactly the same positions. These observations suggest questions to check; they do not prove which difference caused the lower result.

The team plans another attempt using a written folding procedure and marked block positions. It will report the range of results and the conditions used. Repeating the activity may help clarify the pattern, but the next result is not known in advance. A trustworthy report includes inconvenient observations as well as the ones its writers hoped to see.
lessons.title: The Result We Could Not Repeat Yet
